messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] MVPA analysis in children
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] MVPA analysis in children
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bart,

The MVPA output variables from part 2 are not additive, because they try to estimate total time spent in MVPA per day or per week based on different thresholds (bout duration, whether to allow for gaps in bouts, and epoch length). So, you should choose one of them.
Part2 uses by default one specific algorithm (metric) to decide whether to allow for bout gaps, historically originating from the work I did for doi: 10.1093/ije/dyu203.

However, later I realised that an alternative calculation for handling bout gaps is more practical if you want to also characterise light, inactive and vigorous activity in a way that they all can be characterised as non-overlapping categories.
You can activate this alternative calculation (metric) by specifying argument bout.metric=4 in your call to g.shell.GGIR (or g.part2) or by using g.part5 which has bout.metric=4 as a default.

The added value of part5 is that it helps you to split the night time sleep from daytime and it also calculates time spent in light, inactive and vigorous activity. If you are only interested in MVPA and are not concerned about accidentally adding nighttime MVPA (if it exists) then part 2 should be fine.

Best wishes, Vincent

On Fri, 31 Aug 2018 at 10:39, <zalew...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi all!
>
> I am analyzing data from children aged 6-17y, and the outcome of my interest is MVPA over a week. Following the Whitehall II Study reference, I would like to retain activity lasting at least 1 min for which 80% of the activity satisfied the 191.6mg threshold criteria (children).
>
> I am aware of:
> - children threshold criteria for MVPA (based on VT Hildebrand M, VAN Hees VT et al. Med Sci Sports Exerc.2014);
> - the equation to calculate MVPA over a week when less than 7 valid days of data are available:
>  (5xmean daily weekday MVPA time + 2x mean daily week-end MVPA time)/7 (based on Whitehall II Study Menai M, van Hees VT et al. Scientific Reports 2017)
>
> Therefore I plan to use part 2_daysummary.csv, to sum up for a single day of MVPA.:
>
> MVPA_E5S_B1M80%_T191.6_ENMO_0-24hr + MVPA_E5S_B5M80%_T191.6_ENMO_0-24hr + MVPA_E5S_B10M80%_T191.6_ENMO_0-24hr
>
>
> Could you please let me know if this thinking is ok?
> Or shall I use other data? output 5?
>
> I have used GGIR package 1.6.0.
> I used the code as follows:
>
> library(GGIR)
> g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
>              # INPUT NEEDED:
>              mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
>              datadir="xxx",
>              outputdir="xxx",
>              f0=1, f1=2,
>              #-------------------------------
>              # Part 1:
>              #-------------------------------
>              # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
>              do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,
>              chunksize=1,                printsummary=TRUE,
>              #-------------------------------
>              # Part 2:
>              #-------------------------------
>              strategy = 2,               ndayswindow= 4,
>              hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
>              maxdur = 0,                 includedaycrit = 16,
>              winhr = c(5,10),
>              qlevels = c(),
>              qwindow = c(0,24),
>              ilevels = c(),
>              mvpathreshold = c(191.6),
>              bout.metric = 2,
>              closedbout = FALSE,
>              desiredtz="Europe/Warsaw",
>              #-------------------------------
>              # Part 3:
>              #-------------------------------
>              # Key functions: Sleep detection
>              timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
>              ignorenonwear = TRUE,
>              #-------------------------------
>              # Part 4:
>              #-------------------------------
>              # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
>              # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
>              excludefirstlast = TRUE,
>              includenightcrit = 16,
>              def.noc.sleep = c(),
>              loglocation= c(),
>              outliers.only = TRUE,
>              criterror = 4,
>              relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
>              sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
>              colid=1,
>              coln1=2,
>              do.visual = TRUE,
>              nnights = c(),
>              #-------------------------------
>              # Part 5:
>              # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
>              #-------------------------------
>              threshold.lig = c(56.3), threshold.mod = c(191.6),  threshold.vig = c(695.8),
>              boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
>              boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
>              boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),   timewindow = c("WW"),
>              #-----------------------------------
>              # Report generation
>              #-------------------------------
>              # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
>              do.report=c(2,5),
>              visualreport=TRUE,     dofirstpage =TRUE,
>              viewingwindow= 1)
>
> Thank you!
> Bart Zalewski

On Sunday, 19 August 2018 16:36:43 UTC+1, Vincent van Hees wrote:
> Hi Christopher,
> You are on the right path. The exported files are what you need, but I seem to have forgotten to document what those levels refer to.
> I have now created an issue for it: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues/107
> For the time being:
>
> 0 = Sleep period time + sleep
> 1 = Sleep period time + wakefulness (minimal movement)
> 2 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + light activity
> 3 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + moderate activity
> 4 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + vigorous activity
> 5 = Daytime + sustained inactivity
> 6 = Daytime + other inactivity
> 7 = Daytime + light activity
> 8 = Daytime + moderate activity
> 9 = Daytime + vigorous activity
> If you use three bout duration for MVPA, inactive, and light bouts then levels 10 to 18 will look as follows:
> 10 = Daytime + MVPA bout, long length (whichever length you specified)
> 11 = Daytime + MVPA bout, medium length (whichever length you specified)
> 12 = Daytime + MVPA bout, short length (whichever length you specified)
> 13 = Daytime + Inactivity bout, long length (whichever length you specified)
> 14 = Daytime + Inactivity bout, medium length (whichever length you specified)
> 15 = Daytime + Inactivity bout, short length (whichever length you specified)
> 16 = Daytime + Light activity bout, long length (whichever length you specified)
> 17 = Daytime + Light activity bout, medium length (whichever length you specified)
> 18 = Daytime + Light activity bout, short length (whichever length you specified)
>
> As you see the number of bout levels depends on the number of bout durations you choose in the part5.
> I suppose it would be good if the meaning of all these levels is reflected in the column name.
>
> Thanks for raising this gap in the documentation, Vincent
>
>
> On Wed, 15 Aug 2018 at 19:05, <chris...@project-sapiens.com> wrote:
> > Hi All,
> >
> > I am looking to get an activity classification (asleep, awake, active period longer than 10, vigorous activity with active period) as a function of time.

messages.subject: problem loading CSV file in GGIR v. 1.6-0
messages.subject_clean: problem loading CSV file in GGIR v. 1.6-0
messages.body_plain:
I was having trouble loading CSV files created in Actilife when using GGIR v. 1.6-0. These are files I previously analyzed in GGIR v. 1.5-21. I just tried running GGIR v. 1.5-24, and it is working.

The error message I was getting is:

Loading block: 1Error in data.table::fread(filename, nrow = 2, skip = 10, dec = ",", showProgress = FALSE,   :
  Expected sep (' ') but new line, EOF (or other non printing character) ends field 0 when detecting types from point 0: 0, 0, 0^M
Calls: g.shell.GGIR ... g.calibrate -> g.readaccfile -> as.data.frame ->
<Anonymous>
Execution halted

(The 0, 0, 0 just happens to be the first line of axis data for this case. Other files have different values showing.)

I did try dos2unix for some files, and ran GGIR v. 1.6-0 again, thinking there might have been some problem with the end of line character, but that did not solve the problem.

The problem seems to be related to use of data.table::fread in place of read.csv, as noted in the NEWS for version 1.6-0:
"Read functionality for Actigraph csv files speeded up by replacing read.csv by data.table::fread".

Hi Vincent et al.,

Thank you for much for creating and maintaining the GGIR package for accelerometer data analysis. One of my colleagues is currently collecting 24-hour data using GENEActiv at hip position among infants and she'd like to know if it is possible for her to run GGIR as well with her dataset? We know that the sleep algorithm was developed based on wrist-acceleration (i.e. changes in arm degree); therefore it might not be suitable for analysis of hip dataset? Is there a way for her to analyse the sleep data using this package as well?

Thanks.

Best regards,
John.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent et al.,

I just started using GGIR to process my GENEActiv 24-hour dataset (with the following codes) and have encountered a few problems in regard to the summary output:

g.shell.GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4), datadir="/", outputdir="/", f0=1, f1=2, do.enmo = TRUE, do.anglez=TRUE, chunksize=1, printsummary=TRUE, strategy = 1, ndayswindow=6, hrs.del.start = 0, hrs.del.end = 0, maxdur = 7,includedaycrit = 16, winhr = c(5,10), qwindow=c(0,24), dayborder=0, desiredtz="Australia/NSW", timethreshold=5, anglethreshold=5, ignorenonwear=TRUE, excludefirstlast = FALSE, includenightcrit = 16, def.noc.sleep= 1, do.visual = FALSE, nnights =6, timewindow = c("MM"), do.report=c(2,4), visualreport=TRUE, dofirstpage = TRUE, viewingwindow=1)

1) Error in Start Date time stamp
The monitors were initialised to start measurement at midnight i.e. 00:00:00 (Day 1) and therefore the start time for each measurement day should be 00:00:00 given the 24-hour window. However, it turned out that the start time for Day 1 was 1am and then 12.55am for the following days (see below image). I have the same error for all my participants. Could it be that I've missed something in the codes?

2) There's a column in part2_daysummary.csv named 'N valid hours'. Does it refer to the number of valid wear hours after removing the non-wear period from the data? I wonder if there's a specific column in any of the output files where I can get the non-wear duration.  wonder which output file should be referring to if I want to know about the non-wear duration for each day?

3) It seems like the analysis is based on 24-hour window from waking time to waking time but not midnight to midnight? If that's the case does it mean that the sleep time for my Day 1 (from midnight till wake up) was not considered in the analysis? And for other components such as PA were they also analysed based on waking-waking window as well i.e. Day 1 activities (including sleep) reported in the summary csv. were estimated from waking time of Day 1 till waking time of Day 2?

4) I have a participant with wake-up time being detected at 2.28am resulting in a very short sleep duration for that particular day. However when I looked at the summary plot it seems to me that the participant did go back to sleep (with another break in between) till 7ish in the morning. In this case would those time be analysed as sustained inactivity period rather than sleeping time?

Thank you in advance for the help!

Best regards,
John.

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Error in Start Date time stamp and some clarifications about 24-hour window analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

1. Yes, although it may seem odd, I think this is correct. This column is primarily to indicate the date, I may have used the timestamp on which the first large epoch (default 15 minutes) ends. It is a long time ago that I worked on this, but I vaguely remember that I did this to avoid confusion about what date a day belongs: 00:00:00 could be both the beginning and the end of a day.
2. In the part2_summary.csv output you will find: meas_dur_dys, meas_dur_def_proto_day, clipping_score, and wear_dur_def_proto_day. These variables indicate how much data is considered not used (valid) due to: protocol decisions, signal clipping (hardly ever occurs), and monitor non-wear.
3. In part 5 you can request both midnight to midnight and waking time to waking time summary reports (with argument timewindow = c("MM", "WW")). Part4 on the other hand only focuses on the sleep period window, while part 2 only focuses on the window midnight to midnight.
4. Yes - the automated detection of the sleep period time is not perfect as discussed in: See also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-31266-z, which highlights that errors tend to be higher in individuals with disturbed sleep. If you study individuals with known sleep disorders I would advise trying to collect sleep diary information as that would improve your estimates.

Best, Vincent

Yes - the automated detection of the sleep period time is not perfect as discussed in: See also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-31266-z, which highlights that errors tend to be higher in individuals with disturbed sleep. messages.body_plain:
Hi Cathy,
As the function worked for several other GGIR users I assumed that it would be safe to implement it as the default.
1. I am assuming you have package data.table installed, and restarted your R session?

It would be great if you could investigate this a bit more by trying to use function fread from the data.table package directly on your csv files.
For example: data.table::fread("yourfiledirectoryandname.csv", nrow = 2, skip = 10, dec = ",", showProgress = FALSE) should give you the values of two rows in the csv files somewhere around the columns headers.
Next, explore whether different values of nrow, skip, and dec affect the result.
2. What do you see?

3. Is Excel (or other csv editor) able to recognize that the file has three columns or all the data merged into the first column?
4. Are the csv files created on the same machine as on which you are using GGIR?
Vincent
PS: I am doing this without being paid. Please consider my maintenance and support service: https://www.movementdata.nl/how-to-help-sustain-ggir

messages.body_plain:
Hi Christopher,

Good point - this would indeed be a useful enhancement to the reports.

Part 2 produces milestone data (stored as RData file) that includes a time series of when non-wear was detected. See documentation for 'rout' in the GGIR manual, by default at 15 minute resolution.
At line 139 of g.part5 <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/R/g.part5.R> you can see how I currently use this information to only report the total amount of non-wear.

A possible new feature could be to also use the non-wear time in the reports and exported data, e.g. by defining it as a separate category or by leaving the values blank.

You or anyone else interested in this are welcome to work on this software feature and to make a pull request in the GGIR GitHub repository, which I will then merge in addition to making you a package contributor.

If this is too complicated, then I am happy to do this as a paid consultancy as described here: https://www.movementdata.nl/how-to-help-sustain-ggir.

Thanks, Vincent

> > 0 = Sleep period time + sleep
> > 1 = Sleep period time + wakefulness (minimal movement)
> > 2 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + light activity
> > 3 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + moderate activity
> > 4 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + vigorous activity
> > 5 = Daytime + sustained inactivity
> > 6 = Daytime + other inactivity
> > 7 = Daytime + light activity
> > 8 = Daytime + moderate activity
> > 9 = Daytime + vigorous activity
> > If you use three bout duration for MVPA, inactive, and light bouts then levels 10 to 18 will look as follows:
> > 10 = Daytime + MVPA bout, long length (whichever length you specified)
> > 11 = Daytime + MVPA bout, medium length (whichever length you specified)
> > 12 = Daytime + MVPA bout, short length (whichever length you specified)
> > 13 = Daytime + Inactivity bout, long length (whichever length you specified)
> > 14 = Daytime + Inactivity bout, medium length (whichever length you specified)
> > 15 = Daytime + Inactivity bout, short length (whichever length you specified)
> > 16 = Daytime + Light activity bout, long length (whichever length you specified)
> > 17 = Daytime + Light activity bout, medium length (whichever length you specified)
> > 18 = Daytime + Light activity bout, short length (whichever length you specified)
> >
> > As you see the number of bout levels depends on the number of bout durations you choose in the part5.

messages.subject: Non-wear time detection of the final 24 hours
messages.subject_clean: Non-wear time detection of the final 24 hours
messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent!

Within our validation study, we are now analyzing our Geneactiv data (measured over 7 days and 24 hours with 100 Hz). We set up the devices to start measuring on Monday 00:00, and the devices stopped (due to memory capacity) on Sunday 00:00.
Therefore, there was no mailing route or similar and participants brought back the devices on Tuesday or Wednesday. Since we do not have these "final 24 hours", we wonder if the non-wear time detection algorithm (used in the code and described below), may be a problem for us (e.g., erroneously classification of any active time as non-wear time due to the assumption of "device probably on mailing route")? Since the participants wore the devices on the last 24 hours, we do not want to erroneously classify any wear periods as non-wear periods...

“the final 24 hours are often considered the period in which the accelerometer is potentially taken off but moved because of transportation, e.g. by the mail service. All wear-periods in the final 24 hrs of each measurement shorter than three hours and preceded by at least one hour of non-wear time were classified as non-wear. Finally, if the measurement starts or ends with a period of less than three hours of wear followed by non-wear (any length) then this period of wear is classified as non-wear”

Would be great if you can give us some advice!!

Thank you very much for your help and maintaining the GGIR code!!

Best wishes from Graz, Austria!

Matteo Sattler

messages.body_plain:
I am trying to analyse physical activity data collected from geneactiv accelerometer using the GGIR shell function in R (code copied from Accelerometer data processing with GGIR document). The Part 4 section of the code requires comparing the sleep data generated by the accelerometer and a self-reported sleep log. The "loglocation" argument requires you to enter the CSV filename for the manual sleep log. However my study does not include the self-reported sleep log as I am mainly interested in physical activity levels not sleep analysis. How do I modify the code to exclude including the sleep log and get my code to run successfully and produce the necessary visual data? Please find below the R code for physical activity analysis.

    library(GGIR)
    g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
                 # INPUT NEEDED:
                 mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
                 datadir="C:/Hadiza/Documents/GENEACTIV/PAanalysis",
                 outputdir="C:/Hadiza/Documents/GENEACTIV/PAresults",
                 f0=1, f1=2,
                 #-------------------------------
                 # Part 1:
                 #-------------------------------
                 # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
                 do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,
                 chunksize=1,                printsummary=TRUE,
                 #-------------------------------
                 # Part 2:
                 #-------------------------------
                 strategy = 2,               ndayswindow=7,
                 hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
                 maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,
                 winhr = c(5,10),
                 qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
                 qwindow=c(0,24),
                 ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
                 mvpathreshold =c(100,120),
                 bout.metric = 4,
                 closedbout=FALSE,
                 #-------------------------------
                 # Part 3:
                 #-------------------------------
                 # Key functions: Sleep detection
                 timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
                 ignorenonwear = TRUE,
                 #-------------------------------
                 # Part 4:
                 #-------------------------------
                 # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
                 # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
                 excludefirstlast = TRUE,
                 includenightcrit = 16,
                 def.noc.sleep = c(),
                 loglocation= "C:/mydata/sleeplog.csv",
                 outliers.only = TRUE,
                 criterror = 4,
                 relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
                 sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
                 colid=1,
                 coln1=2,
                 do.visual = TRUE,
                 nnights = 9,
                 #-------------------------------
                 # Part 5:
                 # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
                 #-------------------------------
                 threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
                 boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
                 boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
                 boutdur.mvpa = c(1),   timewindow = c("WW"),
                 #-----------------------------------
                 # Report generation
                 #-------------------------------
                 # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
                 do.report=c(2,4,5),
                 visualreport=TRUE,     dofirstpage = TRUE,
                 viewingwindow=1)
